### New

- **Every host now says whether it is there.** A host card used to name the port a host is
  wired to and nothing else. Switching to a sleeping machine, or to one whose cable is out,
  looked exactly like switching to a working one until the screen went blank. The switch
  center, the settings host list and the switcher overlay now carry a standing: **online**
  (filled green), **offline** (grey) and **not checked yet** (hollow). An offline host says
  when it last answered and what the last attempt ran into. Hosts are checked every 30
  seconds while a window is open, and not at all once it is in the tray, so a sleeping host
  is left alone.
- **"Can that host see this display?"** An agent reply now carries the shared displays the
  responder can see on its own side. It answers a question nothing could answer before: the
  host is up, but its cable is out or the display dropped the link while showing another
  host, and switching to it would leave the screen blank. Every matrix cell, every host key
  under a display and every row in the settings list says **seen**, **not seen** or
  **cannot tell**, and explains which on hover. A host that does not report its displays
  reads as unknown, never as "nothing attached".
- **Black and silver join the host colours,** taking the picker from ten to twelve. Silver
  carries its own ink, since the white text every lit surface uses would vanish on it.

### Fixes

- **The wake wait ran past the seconds it promised.** The wait loop treated the configured
  seconds as a number of attempts, and each attempt cost a second of sleep plus however
  long its connect timeout took. Against an unreachable host a 45-second wait ran for over
  two minutes, and the dialog stayed up for all of it. The wait is now a deadline and
  cannot outlast the setting.
- **Hosts reorder by a grip, not by the whole card.** Dragging the card meant a press on
  "Test connection" could turn into a reorder, the host name could not be selected, and
  hovering any button showed the card's "drag to reorder" tooltip. Only the grip on the
  left drags now.
- **The wake-wait setting hardcoded "(45 seconds)"** in its label whatever the field said.
  The label no longer carries a number, and the hint gives the range that actually applies
  (5–120 seconds, 45 by default).
- **A display claimed to be "now showing" a host that could not be seen to have it.** The
  active host is a remembered value that outlives the display being unplugged or put to
  sleep. When the host it names reports that it cannot see the display, the card now reads
  "Last shown" in grey rather than staying lit as though it were confirmed. A paired host
  showing a display this computer cannot read over DDC/CI is the normal case and is
  unchanged.

This release speaks the same protocol as v0.7.2 and pairs and switches with it.

### Known limits

- "Seen / not seen" needs v0.8.0 on both computers. An older host reads as "not reported"
  rather than as an error.
- Black and silver likewise sync only between v0.8.0 hosts; an older host keeps that host's
  default colour.
- Some displays drop the link on hosts they are not showing, and that host then honestly
  reports it cannot see the display. The hint names both causes — the cable, or the dropped
  link — rather than blaming the cable.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed and not yet notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so
  Gatekeeper may ask for it to be allowed by hand.
